title: Hot Cross Buns
subtitle: Spiced enriched buns with a flour cross and fruit
excerpt: Soft, lightly spiced enriched buns packed with mixed fruit and orange zest, topped with a flour paste cross and baked until golden. Glazed while hot and eaten toasted with butter.

recipe.sourceNotes: Hot cross buns have been associated with Good Friday in England since at least the Tudor period, though their exact origin is disputed. Thomas Rockliff is credited with first selling them in London in the late 17th century. The crossed top is thought to symbolise the crucifixion. A London byelaw of 1592 restricted the sale of spiced buns to Good Friday and Christmas, suggesting they were already commercially significant. Today they are sold from January in British supermarkets, but they are still primarily an Easter food. The buns should be soft and pillowy, with a warm spice from cinnamon and mixed spice and a generous proportion of fruit.

content.text: The dough is enriched and therefore slower to rise than a plain bread dough: allow the full time. Do not rush the second prove, as under-proved buns will be dense. The flour cross paste should be thick enough to pipe in a clean line: too thin and it will spread; too thick and it will dry out before baking. Apply the glaze while the buns are hot so it soaks in and sets shiny.

Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, spices, and salt. Rub in the butter. Add the egg and warm milk. Mix to a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Knead in the dried fruit and orange zest. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 equal pieces and shape into smooth balls. Place on a lined baking tray, spaced 3 cm apart. Cover and prove for 45 minutes until well risen and touching.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Mix the plain flour with enough cold water (about 5 to 6 tbsp) to make a thick, smooth paste. Pipe or spoon a cross onto each bun. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Dissolve the 3 tbsp caster sugar in 3 tbsp water in a small pan. Brush immediately over the hot buns. Cool slightly. Slice and toast before eating with cold butter.
